question: In the unsignalized midblock-crosswalk example in Figure 3B-16, how far in advance of the crosswalk are the yield lines shown?
model_answer: Direct Answer: In Drawing B ("Unsignalized midblock crosswalk") of Figure 3B-16, the yield lines are shown 20 to 50 feet in advance of the crosswalk. This matches the recommended placement in Section 2B.19, which states that yield (stop) lines and Yield Here to (Stop Here for) Pedestrians signs should be placed 20 to 50 feet in advance of the nearest edge of the crosswalk on an uncontrolled multi-lane approach. Guidance (recommended): - "If yield (stop) lines and Yield Here to (Stop Here for) Pedestrians signs are used in advance of a crosswalk that crosses an uncontrolled multi-lane approach, the signs should be placed 20 to 50 feet in advance of the nearest edge of the crosswalk (see Section 3B.19 and Figure 3B-16)." Visual evidence: - [Image 1] Figure 3B-16, Drawing B (unsignalized midblock crosswalk) shows a dimension arrow labeled "20 to 50 ft" between the staggered yield lines (with R1-5 signs) and the nearest edge of the marked crosswalk; Drawing C (crosswalk across ramp) also shows a "20 to 50 ft" dimension. - [Image 5] The full-page view of Figure 3B-16 (p.574) confirms the same "20 to 50 ft" dimension in Drawing B between the yield lines and the crosswalk. Citations: - Section 2B.19 Guidance §3 (p.81) - Figure 3B-16 (p.574)
gold_answer: 20 to 50 feet in advance of the crosswalk.
